newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Official of Czech ruling party warns of opposition.
newsitem.headline: Official of Czech ruling party warns of opposition.

text.p: Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec, a top official in the ruling Civic Democratic Party (ODS), called on the party to confront a growing gulf between it and the people.

In a newspaper interview published on Thursday a day before the party's annual congress, Zieleniec, number two in the party structure, said voting in runoff elections to the upper house showed that the joint opposition had to be taken seriously.

"Why was it so easy to create a unified front against the ODS in the second round (of Senate elections)? ... These are things that must be considered if we want the ODS to remain the big player on the right wing," he said in an interview with the daily Lidove Noviny.

The ODS, led by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, took only 32 of 81 seats in the late November runoff to the Senate after vigorous campaigning by the opposition with some support from the ODS's junior coalition partner, the Christian Democrats.
"We have to answer the question: Is not the border beween voters of ODS and its non-voters too sharp?" Zieleniec said.

The ODS annual national congress, to be held on Friday and Saturday in the Czech second city Brno, is scheduled to vote on top officials though Klaus is the only candidate on the ballot for a renewed term as party chairman.
The ODS, a party in which Klaus often tries to emulate the style of former British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher, has controlled Czech politics since winning general elections in 1992.

But Klaus and his coalition lost its majority in parliament in June lower house elections after the left-wing opposition consolidated, putting the centre-left Social Democrats in a strong second-place position.
In a widely-read local newspaper interview in the summer, Zieleniec appealed for more voices to be heard in ODS.
In a thinly-veiled reference to Klaus, Zieleniec implied party leadership was too autocratic.
